title: Deleterious effect of photon-phonon coupling on microcavities in their application as quantum sources
authors: Y. Sacha C. L. S., G. C. Rickli, J. Dipold, R. A. Kögler, Paulo Nussenzveig, Nathália B. Tomazio, M. Martinelli
abstract: In quantum systems, the contact with the environment is detrimental to the purity of the state, thus limiting the practical use of entangled sources in quantum information applications. This loss of purity is observed in the form of additional noise in the tomography of the state. We investigate this noise dependence in $Si_3N_4$ micro-cavities, previously used for quantum state generation, and demonstrate that the dependence of this noise on the temperature is compatible with a coupling of the photonic chips to a thermal reservoir. The control of this noise source is a necessary condition for the efficient implementation of these devices as sources of entangled states in quantum networks.
summary: This paper experimentally characterizes the detrimental effect of photon-phonon coupling on microcavities intended for quantum state generation. By measuring excess phase noise as a function of temperature, the authors confirm that this noise originates from thermal acoustic fluctuations within the crystal lattice. The findings emphasize that controlling this environmental coupling is a necessary prerequisite for utilizing these cavities in robust quantum information applications.
main_problem: The study investigates how photon-phonon coupling introduces excess noise into microcavities, thereby degrading their performance when used as sources for quantum states.
main_result: The observed excess noise is confirmed to be phononic in nature and its temperature dependence allows for the quantification of the coupling rate. Controlling this source of environmental noise is crucial for implementing these devices in quantum networks.
method: The authors analyzed the spectral covariance matrix of the output field, measuring excess phase noise as a function of temperature across different resonant conditions.
model_or_system: The physical system involves $	ext{Si}_3	ext{N}_4$ micro-cavities coupled to a thermal phonon reservoir. The analysis uses input-output formalism and Langevin equations to model the field dynamics, incorporating noise terms from acoustic fluctuations.
key_observables: Excess phase noise power ratio ($\eta$), spectral covariance matrix components ($V(\Omega)$), and temperature coefficients of loss ($\delta\eta/\delta T$).
important_parameters: Temperature dependence ($T$) and driving field power ($P$); the coupling rate was estimated to be proportional to $TP$.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include treating the phonon reservoir as unaffected by the electromagnetic field, ignoring parametric processes below threshold, and simplifying acoustic correlation functions.
figures_summary: Figures show spectral matrix components measurements for multiple cavities under different resonance conditions ($R1$ and $R2$), illustrating noise power ratios versus temperature dependence.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework using input-output formalism to measuring excess noise, quantifying its temperature dependence across two distinct resonant conditions, and concluding with recommendations for noise mitigation in quantum network applications.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses decoherence mechanisms (phonon coupling) in solid-state photonic platforms used for generating entangled states, which is a core challenge in practical quantum networking and quantum optics.

Noise power has the electronic noise subtracted and is normalized to the standard quan- tum limit by the shot noise level measurement. The continuous line is the adjustment of Equation 18. Analysis frequency of 20 MHz, cavity bandwidth of 4 MHz.

Micro-ring (b) has a height of 390 𝜇m and a width of 540 𝜇m. The white pads are contacts of the platinum wire. Once the contacts run a current, the cavity can be tuned into resonance (c), and some scattering from the surface of the waveguide can be observed. The inter- action length between the bus waveguide and the cavity waveguide is about 200 𝜇m.

In the graphs in the bottom row, the actual char- acterizations of the coupling regime show phase inversions in the overcoupled case when depletion crosses the dashed red line.
